messages.subject: Models not compatible for AIC
parts:
Hello everyone,

I understand the explanation is given here (https://rdrr.io/cran/secr/man/AIC.secr.html) as to why would someone encounter this issue but I never got a warning before when I was using secr 3.6 version on the same dataset that I am using now (running the same set of hybrid mixture models). 
 
Just to give some context - my camera trap data has 44 individuals (female =19, male=24, and 1 unknown sex), of which 41 were captured more than once and 18 individuals were captured at least 10 times.


STR_2017.reduce <- reduce(STR_2017, by='ALL')

STR2017_Mod_0   <- secr.fit(STR_2017.reduce, hcov="sex", model=list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), detectfn=0, mask=STR2017_mask, method = "Nelder-Mead")
STR2017_Mod_g0 <- secr.fit(STR_2017.reduce, hcov="sex", model=list(D~1, g0~b, sigma~1), detectfn=0, mask=STR2017_mask, method = "Nelder-Mead")  
STR2017_Mod_s   <- secr.fit(STR_2017.reduce, hcov="sex", model=list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~h2), detectfn=0, mask=STR2017_mask, method = "Nelder-Mead")
STR2017_Mod_g   <- secr.fit(STR_2017.reduce, hcov="sex", model=list(D~1, g0~h2, sigma~1), detectfn=0, mask=STR2017_mask, method = "Nelder-Mead")
STR2017_Mod_sg <- secr.fit(STR_2017.reduce, hcov="sex", model=list(D~1, g0~h2, sigma~h2), detectfn=0, mask=STR2017_mask, method = "Nelder-Mead")


AIC(STR2017_Mod_0, STR2017_Mod_g0, STR2017_Mod_s, STR2017_Mod_g, STR2017_Mod_sg)
                                                    model                             detectfn      npar         logLik          AIC             AICc         dAICc      AICcwt
STR2017_Mod_g0      D~1 g0~b sigma~1 pmix~h2        halfnormal      5       -723.4169    1456.834    1458.413      0.000          1
STR2017_Mod_s        D~1 g0~1 sigma~h2 pmix~h2      halfnormal      5       -740.9162    1491.832    1493.411      34.998         0
STR2017_Mod_0        D~1 g0~1 sigma~1 pmix~h2        halfnormal      4       -742.4088    1492.818    1493.843      35.430        0
STR2017_Mod_g        D~1 g0~h2 sigma~1 pmix~h2      halfnormal      5       -741.4321    1492.864    1494.443      36.030        0
STR2017_Mod_sg      D~1 g0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2    halfnormal      6       -740.8622    1493.724    1495.995      37.582        0
Warning message:
In AIC.secr(STR2017_Mod_0, STR2017_Mod_g0, STR2017_Mod_s, STR2017_Mod_g,  :
  models not compatible for AIC


AICcompatible(STR2017_Mod_0, STR2017_Mod_g0, STR2017_Mod_s, STR2017_Mod_g, STR2017_Mod_sg)
  data         CL     groups   hcov     binomN 
 FALSE   TRUE   TRUE   TRUE    FALSE


I am not sure as to why I was able to compare them before but not anymore? Why binomN and data are showing as false? Do we not specify binomN only for detectors that are of type ‘count’, ‘polygon’, or ‘transect’? If I can't compare these models then how do I pick my best model? I would really appreciate some help or guidance. 

Thank you,
Saloni Salaria

messages.author: 1bc9363092580d4e
messages.subject: Re: Models not compatible for AIC
parts:
Hi Solani,

My suspicion is that your issue lies with the changes that occurred during the development of SECR 4.0 (vignette found here: https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-version4.pdf ). There were several changes during this version update, many of which were aimed at improving the processing speeds of model fitting. In versions 4.0 and later, data is automatically compressed in two ways, one of which specifies that "Binary data for a particular animal and detector over s occasions are summed and modeled as a binomial count of size s on a single occasion". 

Dr. Efford may be able to shed further light on the error you're experiencing, but I think your issue may have something to do with the initial reduce step you have taken, it may no longer be necessary? If you haven't already, perhaps read the SECR 4.0 vignette and you may be able to adjust your code accordingly to provide a solution. More specifically, if you set "details = list(fastproximity = FALSE)" this will be closer to fitting the models as in version 3.2, so maybe give that a go.


Anyways, I'm certainly not an expert but these are some of the things that I have tried with success when using versions 4.0 and later. Hopefully that helps.


Rory

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Models not compatible for AIC
parts:
I think Rory is right, with these additional notes
- fastproximity = TRUE (compression of binary proximity data to single-occasion count proximity data) is the default EXCEPT when the model does not allow it, and g0~b is one case
- the check on compatibility has only been included since secr 4.1.0 (December 2019)

You can either fit all models with details = list(fastproximity = FALSE) or exclude the one with a between-occasion aspect.

Murray
